notes.text: About to take, &c. — It is supposed, (tho' not expressly revealed) that Elijah flourished about twenty years, before he was translated, body and soul, to heaven, only undergoing such a change, as was necessary to qualify him for being an inhabitant in that world of Spirits. By translating him, God gave in that dark and degenerate age, a very sensible proof of another life, together with a type of the ascension of Christ, and the opening of the kingdom of heaven to all believers.

Tarry here — This he desires, either,

1. That being left alone, he might better prepare himself for his great change. Or,

2. Out of indulgence to Elisha, that he might not be overwhelmed with grief at so sad a sight. Or,

3. That he might try his love, and whet his desire to accompany him; it being highly convenient for God's honour, that there should be witnesses of so glorious a translation. To Beth-el - Which was truth, tho' not the whole truth: for he was to go a far longer journey. But he was first to go to Beth-el, as also to Jericho, to the schools of the prophets there, that he might comfort, and strengthen their hearts in God's work, and give them his dying counsels.

glossa.text: *It came to pass. ((RAB. in lib. Reg., t. III.))* A whirlwind, that is, a most violent wind, etc., *as far as* The Lord was taken up, neither begetting by intercourse nor begotten.

notes.text: Night — Which to others was a time of rest and quietness.

glossa.text: *I cried to the Lord with my voice.* ((AUG.)) With the intention of devotion toward the Lord, seeking nothing else from him, because he is Lord, and because he is God. *My voice unto him.* The voice is for this, for the sake of which it is uttered; this he adds, lest he be thought to cry to God for anything else than for himself, above whom there is nothing. ((CAS.)) He does not say what he asks, because there is no need that it be said to him who knows what is expedient. *He hath attended to me.* ((CAS.)) *For God to attend* is to give the whole of what is asked, and more than is asked.

*In the day of my trouble I sought.* ((AUG.)) How didst thou seek? etc., *as far as* he who does not do justice before men, that he may be seen. *He refused to be comforted.* ((ID.)) He expounds the tribulation, etc., *as far as* he who in all men either finds or fears a scandal, is secure in none.

notes.text: Stand fast therefore in the liberty — From the ceremonial law. Wherewith Christ hath made us - And all believers, free; and be not entangled again with the yoke of legal bondage.

The days are fulfilled that he should be received up — That is, the time of his passion was now at hand. St. Luke looks through this, to the glory which was to follow. He steadfastly set his face - Without fear of his enemies, or shame of the cross, Heb. xii, 2.
He sent messengers to make ready — A lodging and needful entertainment for him and those with him.
His face was as though he would go to Jerusalem — It plainly appeared, he was going to worship at the temple, and thereby, in effect, to condemn the Samaritan worship at Mount Gerizim.

As Elisha did — At or near this very place, which might put it into the minds of the apostles to make the motion now, rather than at any other time or place, where Christ had received the like affront.
Ye know not what manner of spirit — The spirit of Christianity is. It is not a spirit of wrath and vengeance, but of peace, and gentleness, and love.
Matt. viii, 19.
But Jesus said to him — First understand the terms: consider on what conditions thou art to follow me.
Suffer me first to bid them farewell that are in my house — As Elisha did after Elijah had called him from the plough, 1 Kings xix, 19; to which our Lord's answer seems to allude.
Is fit for the kingdom of God — Either to propagate or to receive it.

glossa.text:
*Lord, wilt thou. ((BED.))* The apostles, still rude and ignorant of the measure of vengeance, etc., *as far as* such a power has been conferred by God upon holy men.

*We say that fire come down from heaven.* At the word of these men fire would come down from heaven, because they are the sons of thunder. *And consume them? And turning he rebuked them and said.* In the likeness of Elias, who both by his own hand and by fire divinely obtained put the elders of Baal to death. And in this, that the apostles presume to themselves the power of such a prophet, it is shown that the merit of the prophets was in them.

((AMBR.)) The apostles do not sin, who follow the law, etc., *as far as* he does not seek vengeance who does not fear.
*You know not of what spirit you are.* By whose spirit you have been sealed, whose deeds you imitate, now taking counsel mercifully, but in the future judging justly.

*The Son of man came not to destroy souls, but to save,* etc. Perfect virtue has no zeal for vengeance, nor is there any anger where there is the fulness of charity.

((BED.)) Vengeance is not always to be taken upon those who sin, etc., *as far as* from whom in this place the fire is kept back.
*A certain man said. ((ID.))* This man, moved by the greatness of the signs, wishes to follow, etc., *as far as* and he feigned the service of a disciple, which feigning is figured by the fox.

*The foxes have holes. ((ID.))* The fox is a deceitful animal, intent upon ambushes, practising the robberies of fraud, dwelling in holes even amid the very lodgings of men: so the heretic, not having the house of faith, draws others into his own fraud and seduces them from the faith.

*And he said to another.* Note that the Lord spurned not faults but frauds, because he who rejected the fraudulent man chose the innocent one; but him whose father he knew to be dead, that father of whom it is said: *Forget thy father's house ((Psal. XLIV))*, etc.
*Suffer that the dead. ((BED.))* Mystically. The son is not called back from his duty to his father, etc., *as far as* he ought not to bury the devil's treacheries in himself.

*To take leave of those.* If a disciple about to follow God is rebuked because he wishes to take leave of his house, what will become of those who often, with no profit, visits the houses of their own people which they had forsaken.

notes.text: The son, &c. — That is, his grand-son, for he was the son of Jehosaphat, 2 Kings ix, 2. This was intended as a prediction that by these God would punish the degenerate Israelites, plead his own cause among them, and avenge the quarrel of his covenant.
To thee — Thou dost not need me or my service, nor art capable of any advantage from it.

But — I bear a singular respect and love to all saints, for thy sake, whose friends and servants they are, and whose image they bear. This more properly agrees to David, than to Christ, whose goodness was principally designed for, and imparted to sinners.

Sorrows — Having shewed his affection to the servants of the true God, he now declares what an abhorrency he has for those that worship idols. Offerings - In which the Gentiles used sometimes to drink part of the blood of their sacrifices. Names - Of those other gods mentioned before.

The Lord — I rejoice in God as my portion, and desire no better, no other felicity. Cup - The portion which is put into my cup, as the ancient manner was in feasts, where each had his portion of meat, and of wine allotted to him. Lot - My inheritance divided to me by lot, as the custom then was.
Lines — My portion, which was measured with lines. Are fallen - In a land flowing with milk and honey, and above all, blessed with the presence and knowledge of God.

The Lord — Hath inspired that wisdom into me, by which I have chosen the Lord for my portion, and am so fully satisfied with him. Reins - My inward thoughts and affections, being inspired and moved by the Holy Spirit. Instruct - Direct me how to please God, and put my whole trust in him. Night - Even when others are asleep, my mind is working upon God, and improving the silence and solitude of holy meditations.

I have set — I have always presented him to my mind, as my witness and judge, as my patron and protector. Hitherto David seems to have spoken with respect to himself, but now he is transported by the spirit of prophecy, and carried above himself, to speak as a type of Christ, in whom this and the following verses were truly accomplished. Christ as man did always set his father's will and glory before him. Right-hand - To strengthen, protect, assist, and comfort me: as this assistance of God was necessary to Christ as man. Moved - Though the archers shoot grievously at me, and both men and devils seek my destruction, and God sets himself against me as an enemy, yet I am assured he will deliver me out of all my distresses.

My glory — My tongue, which is a man's glory and privilege, above all other living creatures. Rejoiceth - Declares my inward joy. For this word signifies not so much eternal joy, as the outward demonstrations of it. My flesh - My body shall quietly rest in the grave. Shall rest - in confident assurance of its incorruption there, and of its resurrection to an immortal life: the flesh or body is in itself, but a dead lump of clay; yet hope is here ascribed to it figuratively, as it is to the brute creatures, Rom. viii, 19.

Hell — In the state of the dead. Holy one - Me thy holy son, whom thou hast sanctified and sent into the world. It is peculiar to Christ, to be called the holy one of God. To see - To be corrupted or putrefied in the grave, as the bodies of others are.

Life — Thou wilt raise me from the grave, and conduct me to the place and state of everlasting felicity. Presence - In that heavenly paradise, where thou art gloriously present, where thou dost clearly and fully discover the light of thy countenance; whereas in this life thou hidest thy face and shewest us only thy back-parts. Right-hand - Which he mentions as a place of the greatest honour, the place where the saints are placed at the last day, and where Christ himself is said to sit, chap. cx, 1. Pleasures - All our joys are empty and defective: But in heaven there is fulness of joy. Our pleasures here are transient and momentary; but those at God's right hand are pleasures forevermore. For they are the pleasures of immortal souls, in the enjoyment of an eternal God. David appealing to God for his integrity, begs for defense against his enemies, ver. 1-9. Describes their wickedness, ver. 10- 12. Prays for deliverance from them, and rests in hope, ver. 13-15. A prayer of David.

glossa.text: *The inscription of a title.* ((CASS.)) This title is taken from the Gospel, not from the Old Testament. What the title noted, that is, victory and kingdom, belongs to Christ, and that is what is treated of here.

*Preserve me,* etc. The second psalm, which touches briefly on the passion and the resurrection; first, Christ, showing the one nature of man, asks to be preserved, saying that all that he endured has been brought through to the glory of his inheritance. ((AUG.)) Christ speaks here according to his manhood, of whom the royal title stood out in the passion: *Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews.--Of my goods,* etc. ((CASS.)) If God has no need of the goods of Christ the man, but Christ the man has all things from him, the arrogance of men is overthrown, and the heresy of the Pelagians, who think that anything is done by their own good powers.

*To the saints who are in the land. ((Ibid.))* Christ has now set out how he prayed; he now tells what good things God did for him. ((AUG.)) *To the saints,* etc., *as far as* and power that I might rise again.

*He hath made wonderful.* ((CASS.)) As if to say, these things I said to the Lord: but the Lord made them wonderful, that is, he made my wills wonderful; and they are wonderful in that those who obey them become heavenly out of earthly.
*They are multiplied. ((Ibid.))* Whereby he made them wonderful, etc., *as far as* which sound together in one note, by which his wills are shown.

*The portion of my inheritance.* ((AUG.)) Let others choose other things, etc., *as far as* but those who choose God as their portion. ((CASS.)) Or, *the Lord* is the *portion,* that is, the share and the reward, *of my inheritance,* that is, of the saints. And *the portion of my cup,* that is, the wage of the passion. For the inheritance belongs to the Gentiles, the cup to the passion, which when drunk gives resurrection. But let no one think himself an heir save he that is illustrious.

*The lines,* etc. ((Ibid.)) As it were by lot, in which is the divine election, as the lot also fell upon Matthias, and each man takes according to his own measure. *In goodly places.* That is, among the saints.

*I will bless the Lord. ((Ibid.))* He gives thanks to the Father for understanding, and for the passion, in which by his favour he conquers, and for the resurrection, and for confession; and these are the things through which the inheritance is restored, so that he is king of the Jews, as the title says. *Understanding,* etc. ((AUG.)) Whereby this inheritance can be seen and possessed. *Moreover,* etc. That is, above understanding. *Even till night,* etc. That is, till death, he hath instructed me, that is, my lower part, the assumption of flesh, that he might drive out the darknesses of mortality which that understanding does not have, because for them it could neither be troubled nor fail. *My reins.* From whom according to the flesh I came forth, namely my kindred: they have chided me with injuries, with temptation and with passion.
*I set the Lord before me. ((Ibid.))* From this draw an example, whereby sins may be shunned: for he who always beholds God with the keen edge of the mind is not bowed down by sins.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Jesus set his face toward Jerusalem, and he calls us to the road.
We will follow you, wherever you go.
No looking back now, no hand lifted from the plow.
Lead us, and we will not turn aside.
Your way was through the sea, your path through the mighty waters.
Yet you led your people like a flock.
Come, take up the journey and worship.
We set out after Jesus. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Elisha watched the mantle fall from the sky, picked it up off the ground, and turned back to the river — the road was his now.
Lead us, and we will follow.
Jesus set his face toward Jerusalem, steady as flint, and the way was long and the cost was real, and still he walked it.
Lead us, and we will follow.
He says, leave the dead to bury the dead, put your hand to the plow and don't look back — the kingdom is up ahead.
Lead us, and we will follow.
Your way once cut a path straight through the sea; you have never lost your people on the road. So we set out. Walk with us.
Lead us, and we will follow. Amen.

lines: Jesus set his face toward Jerusalem.

Lead us, and we will follow. Amen.
